findings.title: No re-check of the cache after taking the write lock
findings.body: The cache is read under RLock, the lock is released, and the write Lock is taken afterwards without checking the cache again. On a cold start in non-dev mode, N concurrent requests all see nil. They then queue on Lock(), and each one in turn reads and parses assets-manifest.json and re-applies the CDN URL, even though the first one already filled the cache. The result is correct but the work is redundant, and every request waits behind that serialized I/O. Re-checking `entryPointAssetsCache != nil && cfg.Env != setting.Dev` right after acquiring the write lock avoids this.

findings.title: No regression test for the race being fixed
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race but adds no test. A test that calls GetWebAssets from several goroutines and is run with `-race` would show the race is gone and keep it from coming back. It could also check that the cache is populated once in non-dev mode.
